top.title: Hands-on jewellery workshop empowers blind participant
top.snippet:
Jewellery designer Richard Allen, owner of Yorkshire based-Pepper Tree Studio, has demonstrated that jewellery is all about inclusivity. Recently welcoming a blind participant to a one-to-one silver jewellery-making workshop, Allen helped her to create a silver pendant. As reported on by the NAJ, Bex is totally blind and has wanted to learn traditional silversmithing techniques […]

es.title: Taller práctico de joyería empodera a participante ciego
es.summary: El diseñador de joyas Richard Allen de Pepper Tree Studio organizó un taller de fabricación de joyas de plata uno a uno para un participante ciego, demostrando inclusividad en la industria. El participante, Bex, que es completamente ciego, pudo aprender técnicas tradicionales de platería y crear un colgante de plata.

oneSentenceSummary: Despite AI's sky-high paper valuations, persistent struggles to monetize models expose a rift between technological optimism and commercial reality.
editorialTake:
AI’s gold rush is colliding with the reality that scale alone does not guarantee profit. Amazon’s $200bn AI spending spree aims to claw back AWS market share from Microsoft and Google, while OpenAI and Anthropic chase ever-higher valuations and revenue targets, yet neither has cracked sustainable monetization. Shopify, by contrast, is quietly using AI to drive a 30% revenue surge through B2B sales and new commerce tools, showing that integrating AI into practical, merchant-facing products pays off faster than headline-grabbing model launches.

Luxury and jewellery operators should not be distracted by the spectacle of AI arms races or sky-high valuations. Hermès’ 9.8% quarterly growth and Nordstrom’s loyalty push both show that customer experience and product innovation, not tech hype, drive real sales. The strongest objection is that AI’s commercial impact is just delayed, but Shopify’s results prove that value comes from targeted, operational applications, not abstract scale.

For the next quarter, I would prioritize AI that improves service, personalizes journeys, or supports new product lines, especially as shoppers return to stores and expect more from in-person and digital touchpoints. Watch for tools that make teams faster or smarter, not just bigger models.
